full_judgment: 2. Plaintiff is the appellant. He filed Other Suit No. 25 of 1979 in the court of Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong for a decree of specific performance of contract for sale of land. It was stated in the plaint that the suit land measuring 0.08 sataks (4 gondas) of RS Plot No. 397, Khatian No. 117 of Mouza Alam Shah belongs to respondent No. 1, Sri Sri Chatteswari Devi Bigraha, the deity. Respondent Nos. 1 (a) to (e) are the Shebaits of the said deity. In 1972 Chatteswari Mandir Unnayan Committee comprising some local persons and Shebaits was formed Respondent Nos. 1 (a) and 1(b) are the Secretary and the Joint Secretary of the Committee respectively which was formed in 1972. As the temple was damaged in 1971 the Shebaits wanted to sell the suit land for repairing the temple. Appellant offered to purchase the same. On 8th May 1977 the aforesaid Committee unanimously passed resolution of the sale of land surrounding the temple for its development and preservation. In all eight persons attended the meeting. Respondent Nos. 1(a) to 1(e) are parties to the resolution. On 16th July, 1977 the Committee held a meeting where in the resolution was unanimously adopted. Value of the land was fixed at Taka 13,000 per ganda. On 25th July 1977 an agreement for sale was executed by respondent Nos. 1(a) to 1(b) and respondent Nos. 1(c), 1(d) and 1(e) also signed the agreement, but as witnesses attesting the execution of the document. Appellant paid Taka 5,000 in cash. On several occasions appellant requested respondent Nos. 1(a) to 1(e) to execute the sale deed. After deferring the matter they refused to execute and register the sale deed on 31st January 1979. Respondent No. 1(a) admitted the claim of the appellant in the written statement filed by him wherein he stated that the sale deed could not be executed amicably as some of the Shebaits are not willing to do it.
